findings.issue: The fixture-consistency loop never checks that each case's stored method follows the A-4 rule (estimateEvaluations(combos, boardSize) <= exhaustiveLimit exactly when method is 'exhaustive'). Only mw-* are asserted exhaustive. A hand-edited fixture that relabelled a case's method would pass every test.
findings.evidence: Lines 77-89 check sums, equity rounding, seed/method pairing and mw-* exhaustive, but not the A-4 rule. estimateEvaluations is already imported (line 9) and used only to pick the smallest case.
findings.fix: Inside the per-case loop add: expect(c.method === 'exhaustive', c.id).toBe(estimateEvaluations(c.combos, parseCards(c.board).length) <= EXHAUSTIVE_LIMIT).

findings.issue: The change is 812 lines against a 750-line scope budget. The generator is 371 lines against an estimate of about 260.
findings.evidence: gates/fix-2.json changed_lines 812. Most of the extra lines come from the separate exhaustive/sampled/dealExists functions and JSDoc typedefs. None of it is dead code.
findings.fix: No code change is needed. Record the overrun and its reason in the build log or judge notes. If trimming is wanted: dealExists duplicates the exhaustive() DFS, but it is needed before sampling, so keep it.

findings.issue: resolve() re-implements the generator's resolveOpponent. This is defensible because it keeps the locked acceptance test independent of tools/, and the combos check catches any drift.
findings.fix: Leave as is, or import resolveOpponent with a lib object as the unit test does.

findings.issue: The spec's rule 4 says 'Preflop range cases come out high-sample'. rr-b0-05 and rr-b0-17 are exhaustive. This is correct under the A-4 formula: 24 x C(48,5) x 2 = 82.2M and 20 x C(48,5) x 2 = 68.5M, both <= 100M, and the stored trials 41,095,296 = 24 x 1,712,304 and 34,246,080 = 20 x 1,712,304 match. The spec wording is the inaccurate part, not the code.
findings.evidence: rr-b0-09 (33 combos) = 113M > 100M is high-sample, which confirms the threshold is applied correctly.
findings.fix: No code change. Optionally note in the story doc that 2 single-opponent preflop range cases are exhaustive under A-4.

summary: All SPEC items are implemented and the tests are strong. The generator imports only generate-reference.js (enumerateExact, mulberry32, cardText), ranges.ts, cards.ts and hand-evaluator.ts. ranges.ts imports only a type from equity.ts, so the references are not circular. Both paths use the D-1 model: exhaustive covers every compatible deal and then every runout; sampled draws a uniform combo per opponent, rejects the whole deal on any clash, and then draws a uniform runout. The A-4 method choice is correct for every case checked, including rr-b0-05 and rr-b0-17. Reference standard error is <= 0.035 pp at 2M trials. The largest observed error is 0.870 pp (rr-b5-04: exhaustive reference vs the 30k-sample calculator, about 3.5 calculator SE) against the 1.5 pp tolerance. I regenerated the fixture in a temp copy in 64.4 s and it came out byte-identical. AC#3 truly permutes ranges: all 6 orders of 3 distinct ranges on the sampled path, preflop and flop; reversal for every case with >= 2 opponents; and an A-7 swap where X' differs from X, compared with whole-result toStrictEqual. The 7 new tests take 2.45 s. Typecheck and lint pass, there are no network imports, and src/ is unchanged. There are no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
